content.title: Identifying Significant Correlates of Adolescent Online Gambling Using A Random Forest Approach: A Cross-Sectional Study
content.abstract: Online gambling is increasing among adolescents. Machine learning methods can be used to identify and rank classification-relevant predictors among a large set of variables. This study identified and ranked factors associated with online gambling among high school students in Canada using a Random Forest (RF) approach. This study used repeat cross-sectional data from Year 6 (2017-18) to Year 8 (2019-20) of the COMPASS study, including n = 103,008 students in grades 9 to 12 from 151 schools in 4 Canadian provinces.
